What El Al Israel Airlines Shares TA 35 Entry Means For Shareholders
sum: El Al Israel Airlines has been added to the TA-35 Index and reported Q3 2026 results, with quarterly sales of US$1,268.9 million and net income of US$172.2 million, alongside nine month sales of US$2,817.4 million and net income of US$229.2 million.
Index inclusion could draw attention from passive funds, while higher sales and lower earnings per share point to shifting cost and profitability pressures for El Al Israel Airlines.
The focus now turns to how El Al Israel Airlines' TA-35 inclusion reshapes its investment narrative and potential investor base.

Spot opportunities around El Al Israel Airlines' TA-35 debut by comparing it with our curated 582 high quality undiscovered gems, which also pair stronger financial profiles with growing investor attention.

To own El Al Israel Airlines, you need to trust that its core aviation business can convert strong demand into durable profitability in a capital heavy sector. TA-35 inclusion puts the airline in front of more institutional and index linked money, yet the latest Q3 2026 report reminds you that higher US$1,268.9 million quarterly sales and US$2,817.4 million nine month revenue have come with pressure on earnings and margins. The big question is whether management can run aircraft, routes, and labor tightly enough for that revenue base to support consistent cash generation.

The near term story hinges on execution and cost control more than headline growth. Net income of US$172.2 million for Q3 and US$229.2 million for the first nine months sits alongside lower earnings per share than a year ago, which keeps attention on efficiency, fleet spending, and balance sheet flexibility rather than rapid expansion. Index entry could help trading liquidity, although it does not change fuel costs, competition, or the capital needs of an airline that already reports high return on equity and high quality earnings but thinner 7.6% margins than last year.

items.t: El Al Israel Airlines (TASE:ELAL) Climbed, But What Is Drawing Attention Now?
sum: El Al Israel Airlines (TASE:ELAL) just posted third quarter 2026 results that paired higher sales with lower profit, a mix that gives you a clear snapshot of the trade off between growth and earnings.

That mixed earnings picture came at a time when momentum has been rebuilding in El Al Israel Airlines shares. The 30 day share price return was 8.77% and the 90 day gain was 19.58%. These contributed to a 1 year total shareholder return of 32.95% and a very large 5 year total shareholder return, all based on a latest share price of ₪19.48.

After a run to ₪19.48 on mixed earnings, the real tension around El Al Israel Airlines now sits in the gap between that price and fair value estimates. How wide is that spread, and which side does the risk lean toward?
Preferred P/E of 11.8x for El Al Israel Airlines: Is it justified?
On valuation, the spotlight falls on earnings. El Al Israel Airlines trades on a P/E of 11.8x, while our DCF model points to a future cash flow value of ₪6.45 against the current ₪19.48 share price.

The P/E multiple tells you how much investors are paying for each unit of net profit. In this case, the market is valuing El Al Israel Airlines at 11.8 times its earnings, which sits above the peer average of 7.2x and below the broader Asian Airlines industry at 14.1x.

That mix sends a split signal. Compared with direct peers, the stock looks expensive, which suggests the market is willing to pay more for its current earnings profile. Against the wider Asian Airlines group, the same P/E appears more restrained, which could imply investors are pricing in a more conservative outlook than the broader regional sector.
